heading: Should I recompress an existing WebP image?
introduction: A new WebP encode can reduce a large website image, but an already efficient WebP may become larger. Compare the actual size and appearance before replacing the version already in use.

sections.heading: Optimize for the display size
sections.body: Add the WebP file, keep WebP output and choose a preset. After processing, inspect the download at the size used by your website. Avoid keeping dimensions far beyond what the page needs.

sections.heading: Keep transparency when you need it
sections.body: WebP can retain transparent areas. Check edges against both light and dark backgrounds after downloading. JPG output is unavailable when a transparent source would have to be flattened.

sections.heading: Keep a result only when it suits the page
sections.body: Compare file size, dimensions and visible detail together. A smaller file with unreadable text may be unsuitable, while an unchanged or larger file may provide no benefit. Preserve the source image for later edits.

seoDescription: Re-encode WebP images locally for website use. Compare file size, dimensions, detail and transparency before replacing an existing image.
